column1: # The shapes of text a published or committed artifact of this repository must never carry.
# One definition, read by every check that looks for them: scripts/ci/no-machine-paths
# (every tracked file), scripts/site-check (the built site) and `majordomus quality rustdoc`
# (the crate's documentation tree, through src/quality/leaks.rs, which compiles this file
# into the executable). Each reader applies the classes it is about; none of them keeps a
# copy of a pattern, because a pattern that lived in three places has already drifted once.
# One pattern per line: <class> TAB <name> TAB <POSIX extended regular expression>.
# The expressions are written in the subset grep -E, git grep -E and the Rust regex crate
# read identically: bracket classes, [[:space:]], alternation, bounded repetition, \b.
# Each is matched against one line at a time, case-sensitively, as grep matches them.
# The classes:
#   machine-path    a path of the machine that wrote the file: a developer's home directory
#                   on macOS, a developer checkout under a Linux home. Deliberately not every
#                   Linux home directory: docs/CLI.md documents a command whose sample output
#                   names a home without a checkout, and a gate that fires on the
#                   documentation of its own tool is a gate somebody switches off.
#   runner-path     the home of a hosted CI runner, where a tree built in CI would record it.
#   private-host    a host name only a private network resolves.
#   credential      a long opaque value assigned to something called a key, a secret, a
#                   token or a password.
#   not-credential  applied to a credential match, not to the text: a match it finds is a
#                   name rather than a value. A reference to the workflow's own token, and a
#                   value that is a SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constant name — letters and
#                   underscores only, so `bytes_per_token` assigned the constant that holds
#                   it is code, while any value carrying a digit or a lower-case letter is
#                   still a credential. The case is spelled out rather than folded because
#                   grep and sed disagree about every way of asking for folding.
machine-path
machine-path
runner-path
private-host

credential
